briefing.opening: Good day. Welcome to the Daily Climate Briefing for November 27, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Accelerating Warming and Global Water Resource and Ecosystem Crises
sections.content: Following record-breaking temperatures in 2023 and 2024, a sharp global rise in temperatures occurred again this November, intensifying the climate crisis [87, 93]. According to a study by the Chinese Academy of Sciences, global freshwater levels have plummeted precipitously over the past two years, making measures to address water depletion caused by climate change and the expansion of AI data centers an urgent priority [1, 93]. Meanwhile, as global glaciers face sustained melting risks regardless of whether net zero is achieved, warnings of ecosystem collapse continue to mount, including heightened risks of extreme wildfires and heatwaves in southern and central Australia and concerns over the disappearance of squid species in domestic waters [73, 76, 92].

sections.title: 🌍 Stalled COP31 Negotiations and International Challenges Surrounding the Fossil Fuel Phase-out
sections.content: At the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), international divisions remain unresolved regarding the phase-out of fossil fuels and the allocation of the enormous costs involved [81, 95]. Criticism has emerged calling for fundamental reform of the COP framework after 31 summits, as even host nation Australia struggles to achieve its 2035 greenhouse gas reduction target due to domestic friction hindering fossil fuel phase-down [14, 77]. Amidst this negotiating stalemate, forest conservation and ecological resilience remain prominent agenda items, with numerous nations and corporations seeking alternative alignments centered on electrification [79, 95].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Renewable Energy Market Overhaul and Power Grid Infrastructure Expansion
sections.content: The government is overhauling the renewable energy market for the first time in 15 years, officially phasing out the solar REC spot market in 2029 and transitioning the market structure toward 20-year long-term fixed-price contracts [44, 46, 59, 62]. As power generation companies shift from simple buyers to direct investors, competitive bidding allocation schemes are also under review to prevent preemptive hoarding of grid capacity [56, 57, 67]. However, with frequent output curtailment resulting from renewable expansion and grid reinforcement costs reaching tens of trillions of won emerging as primary hurdles, establishing a large-scale centralized ESS contract market and implementing power demand-side management have become imperative tasks [45, 48, 55]. Amid these developments, Jeju Province has declared its carbon-neutral vision, aiming to become the world's first 100% renewable energy island by 2035 [26, 47, 52].

sections.title: 🌱 Industry Carbon Neutrality Certification and the Spread of Multilateral and Community-Level Action
sections.content: Multilateral solidarity and carbon-neutral action across industry and local communities are yielding tangible results in addressing the climate crisis. South Korea, China, and Japan discussed cooperative climate response strategies through the Low-Carbon Youth Forum, while six Northeast Asian nations agreed to strengthen cooperation on designating marine protected areas and addressing climate change [5, 9, 22]. In the industrial sector, Bentley Motors set a leading example by completing verification under new international carbon-neutral standards for its Crewe plant in the UK and significantly reducing greenhouse gas emissions [21, 40, 42]. Furthermore, grassroots mitigation efforts led by municipal governments continue to expand, highlighted by Seongbuk-gu's selection as the top district for Eco-Mileage and Jecheon City's awards for Carbon-Neutral Action Villages [23, 33].

briefing.closing: Even amidst global climate disasters and the challenges of the energy transition, progress toward technological and institutional innovation continues. That concludes today's climate briefing.
